pairs.question: Quid vos hanc miseram ac tenuem sectamini praedam, quibus licet iam esse fortunatissimos?
pairs.answer: Tribus horis Aduatucam venire potestis: huc omnes suas fortunas exercitus Romanorum contulit: praesidi tantum est, ut ne murus quidem cingi possit, neque quisquam egredi extra munitiones audeat.
pairs.derivation: A captive (unus ex captivis) poses a real rhetorical interrogative (Quid... sectamini praedam?) and answers it himself within the same continuous utterance. Dropped the speech tag 'inquit' (interleaved as '"Quid vos," inquit, "hanc...'); the question is quoted contiguously across that tag. The answer is the operative following sentences of the same speech, beginning at 'Tribus horis' (which directly responds: stop chasing this plunder because a far richer, near-undefended prize is three hours away) and ending at 'audeat', the last sentence of the utterance before the narration resumes with 'Oblata spe Germani...'.
